note: Program terms checked against the cited official pages on 2026-10-09; 18 records rechecked 2026-10-26 (see each last_verified). Status 'retired' marks a legacy label no official page establishes, kept so older saved deals still resolve; 'see' names the real program. Null means unpublished, ambiguous or unverified, as explained by source_note. review_by is an internal quarterly review reminder, not a program deadline. Published caps and historical allocations are not available balances.

CHFA-HTF.name: CHFA Housing Trust Fund (retired label: no current CHFA program)
CHFA-HTF.description: Not a current CHFA program. CHFA's gap loans are the Housing Opportunity Fund (HOF) and the Capital Magnet Fund (CMF).
CHFA-HTF.source_note: CHFA Flexible Gap Financing page read 2026-10-26: "CHFA's flexible gap programs (CMF and HOF) help with ever-growing project costs". CHFA lists no Housing Trust Fund product; use CHFA HOF (up to $1M, 30 years) or CHFA CMF ($750,000, 17 years).

CHFA-CCLA.name: CHFA Construction/Permanent Loan Advantage (retired label: no current CHFA program)
CHFA-CCLA.description: Not a current CHFA program. CHFA's construction-to-permanent bond loans are CAPABLE and PAIRABLE.
CHFA-CCLA.source_note: CHFA Construction-to-Permanent page read 2026-10-26: "CHFA's construction-to-permanent loans finance larger 4 percent Housing Credit properties using Private Activity Bonds (PAB), structured with CHFA as the senior lender (CAPABLE) or with a construction lender bank partner (PAIRABLE)." No product carries this legacy name.

CHFA-CMF.name: CHFA Capital Magnet Fund
CHFA-CMF.description: CHFA flexible gap financing for eligible 4% or 9% Housing Tax Credit developments. CHFA announced a $4.5 million federal CMF award on November 7, 2024; that award is not a current available balance.
restrictions: CHFA need not be senior lender for the main loan; the optional 20% structure requires CHFA senior financing.

max_rule.text: Up to $750,000 per project; up to 20% may be deferred or granted when CHFA is senior lender, subject to CHFA clarification.

CHFA-CMF.source_note: Main loan requires monthly principal and interest. No numeric interest rate or uncommitted balance is published. CHFA pages disagree on the optional 20% when CHFA is senior lender: the CMF FAQ says a deferred no-interest loan, while the small-loan comparison says a grant. Confirm that portion with CHFA; do not classify the whole loan as a grant. The 17-year term comes from both pages.

DOLA-HTF.name: Colorado DOLA Housing Trust Fund (retired label: no current DOH program)
DOLA-HTF.description: Not a current DOH program. The Division of Housing's own development money is the Housing Development Grant (HDG) and Housing Development Loan Fund (HDLF).
DOLA-HTF.source_note: DOH resources page read 2026-10-26 lists HOME, CDBG, CDBG-DR, Housing Development Grant Funds (HDG), Housing Development Loan Funds (HDLF), PAB, CHIF and Section 811 PRA, and no Housing Trust Fund. The state's own development funds are HDG and HDLF; use the Housing Development Grant.

CDBG-DR.name: CDBG Disaster Recovery (DOLA)
CDBG-DR.description: Disaster recovery money tied to the Marshall Fire allocation. No open rental development round.
CDBG-DR.source_note: DLG CDBG-DR page read 2026-10-26: "Following the Marshall Fire on December 30, 2021," the state "received an initial $7.415 million allocation". The program is real but tied to that disaster, and the page names no open rental development round, so it is a watch item, not available funding.

Denver-AHTF.name: Denver Affordable Housing Trust Fund (retired label: see Denver HOST gap financing)
Denver-AHTF.description: Denver's Dedicated Affordable Housing Fund is paid out through HOST gap financing solicitations. HOST canceled its Fall 2026 round; the next opens in Q1 2027.
Denver-AHTF.source_note: Denver HOST Housing Development Resources page read 2026-10-26: Denver's fund is the Dedicated Affordable Housing Fund, paid out through HOST gap solicitations. "Due to reduced available funding, the 2026 Fall Solicitation Round will be canceled and combined with the 2027 Winter Solicitation Round, which we expect to open in Q1 2027."

Boulder-HTF.name: Boulder County Housing Trust Fund (retired label: no current county program)
Boulder-HTF.description: Not a current Boulder County program. The City of Boulder's Affordable Housing Fund is the local development source.
Boulder-HTF.source_note: Boulder County housing page read 2026-10-26 names no housing trust fund. The City of Boulder Affordable Housing Fund (AHF) is a real local source; it is listed on the Funding Sources tab.

HOME-CO.name: HOME Investment Partnerships (State)
HOME-CO.description: Federal HOME assistance through DOH for eligible rental acquisition, rehabilitation and construction. Award-specific terms must be obtained from DOH.
HOME-CO.source_note: DOH HOME page read 2026-10-26: "Funds are awarded as a grant or loan for housing development and CHDO set-asides." The page lists no round dates; the last development round offering HOME closed July 30, 2026 and no later HOME development round is posted. Funding type, rate, term, repayment and award are award-specific and left blank.

DOH-AHTF.name: DOH Affordable Housing Trust Fund (retired label: no current DOH program)
DOH-AHTF.description: Not a current DOH program. Use the Housing Development Grant (HDG) or Housing Development Loan Fund (HDLF).
DOH-AHTF.source_note: DOH resources page read 2026-10-26 names no Affordable Housing Trust Fund; it duplicates the DOLA-HTF legacy label. Use the Housing Development Grant.

DOH-HDG.name: DOH Housing Development Grant
DOH-HDG.description: DOH Housing Development Grant Funds can be awarded as grants or loans for acquisition, rehabilitation and construction. Use the award-specific terms.
DOH-HDG.source_note: DOH HDG page read 2026-10-26: "Funds are awarded as a grant or a loan." Loan rates "generally 2% for for-profits and 1% for non-profits", term "typically commensurate with senior debt", repayment "typically a percentage of cash flow or up to a 40 year amortization". A single rate or term would mislead, so each is left blank. DOH application schedule read 2026-10-26: January 2027 round, Letter of Intent Deadline: December 1, 2026, Application Deadline: January 15, 2027; April 2027 round, LOI March 16, 2027, application April 30, 2027. No program-wide cap or balance is stated.

DOH-HHPG.name: DOH Homeless Housing Program Grant (retired label: no current DOH program)
DOH-HHPG.description: Not a current DOH program. Supportive housing capital goes through DOH's Creation of Supportive Housing RFA and Prop 123's homelessness program.
DOH-HHPG.source_note: DOH funding page read 2026-10-26 lists "Creation of Supportive Housing" and the "Homelessness Resolution Program (HRP)" (services), and no Homeless Housing Program Grant. Capital for supportive housing goes through the Creation of Supportive Housing RFA (Round D applications due November 2, 2026) and Prop 123 PEH.

NHTF-CO.name: National Housing Trust Fund (Colorado)
NHTF-CO.description: Federal National Housing Trust Fund assistance administered by Colorado DOH for extremely low-income rental housing; grants or loans depend on the award.
NHTF-CO.source_note: DOH HTF page read 2026-10-26: "Housing development with all DOH-assisted units restricted to 30% AMI or lower"; "Funds are awarded as a grant or a loan." No round dates are listed; the last round offering HTF closed July 30, 2026. Funding type, rate, term, repayment and award are left blank.

PROP123-AHTF.name: Proposition 123 State Affordable Housing Fund (umbrella; pick a program)
PROP123-AHTF.description: Proposition 123's State Affordable Housing Fund is split: 60% is overseen by OEDIT and managed by CHFA (the Affordable Housing Financing Fund), and 40% goes to DOLA (the Affordable Housing Support Fund). Rental gap finance, equity and land banking have separate records and award terms. This umbrella entry is not an additional source to sum.
PROP123-AHTF.note: See PROP123-LIHTC-GAP, PROP123-EQUITY and PROP123-LBTF for the distinct instruments.
PROP123-AHTF.source_note: Umbrella record, not a financing source. DOLA Prop 123 page read 2026-10-26 describes one State Affordable Housing Fund: 40% to DOLA (homeownership, homelessness, local planning capacity) and 60% overseen by OEDIT with CHFA (land banking, equity, concessionary debt). Use the specific program: LIHTC Gap Finance, Equity or Land Banking.

PROP123-LBTF.name: Prop 123 Land Banking Trust Fund
PROP123-LBTF.description: Prop 123 land acquisition and preservation through grants to eligible governments or forgivable loans to eligible nonprofits.
restrictions: Rural and Rural Resort applications: September 15 through December 31, 2026, or until funds are exhausted; all geographies from January 2027.
Jurisdiction must have a Proposition 123 affordable-housing commitment.
Land acquisition, not construction gap financing.

max_rule.text: Lesser of $5,000,000 or CHFA concluded appraised value.

PROP123-LBTF.source_note: Grants serve local/tribal governments; forgivable loans serve nonprofits. There is no single funding type, interest rate, loan term or repayment for both, so these are left blank. Nonprofit loans accrue 2% deferred interest, waived if milestones are met: zoning/development plan within 5 years and permits/funding within 10. Missed milestones trigger repayment within six months. The cap is also limited to CHFA appraised value. The FY27 allocation is not an uncommitted balance.

PAB-CO.name: Private Activity Bond Volume Cap (Colorado)
PAB-CO.description: Private Activity Bond volume-cap context. Allocation authority is separate from the actual project bond loan; confirm current availability and qualification with the allocating authority.
PAB-CO.adminEntity: DOLA Division of Housing (Statewide Balance); CHFA and local issuers
PAB-CO.source_note: DOLA PAB page read 2026-10-26: "Round 3, open to any issuing authority and to pipeline requests: Application due date: November 1, 2026", committee decisions December 2026. DOLA 2026 Direct Allocations page: "Private Activity Bond Cap available in 2026: $811,695,735" and "Total cap available to the Statewide Balance: $13,327,048". Volume cap is borrowing authority, not a loan or grant, so funding type, rate, term, repayment and award are blank; balances are not a project award.

OZ-EQUITY.name: Opportunity Zone Equity Investment
OZ-EQUITY.description: Qualified Opportunity Zone (QOZ) capital gains deferral incentive under IRC §1400Z-2. Projects in designated OZ census tracts can attract equity from investors seeking capital gains tax deferral. Can be layered with LIHTC but complex structuring required. Not a direct funding program — availability depends on investor market.
OZ-EQUITY.note: 2018 OZ designations remain relevant through 12/31/2028; OZ 2.0 creates decennial designation rounds beginning with the 2026-07-01 determination date. Rural sites should diligence whether a Qualified Rural Opportunity Fund structure applies; Public Law 119-21 §70421 adds a 30% five-year basis step-up for qualifying rural QROF investments. Projects must be in designated OZ tracts (see QCT/DDA overlay).
OZ-EQUITY.source_note: The CDFI page describes the Opportunity Zone designation and investor tax incentive. It does not state a universal investor interest rate, loan term, repayment schedule, project cap or available balance. Those terms depend on private investment agreements; a blank does not mean free capital.

NMTC-CO.name: New Markets Tax Credits (Colorado CDEs)
NMTC-CO.description: NMTC supports qualifying investments through Community Development Entities. Obtain CDE-specific financing terms and confirm rental/mixed-use eligibility; no universal rental project award is assumed.
NMTC-CO.note: NMTC + LIHTC dual structures are rare but possible for mixed-use developments with commercial components.
NMTC-CO.source_note: CDFI Fund NMTC page read 2026-10-26: "Opening Date September 17, 2026 Deadline November 10, 2026 Announcement Date Fall 2027". That round is for Community Development Entities; a project seeks NMTC financing from a CDE with allocation. Funding type, rate, term, repayment and award are set by the CDE and left blank. The seven-year credit period is not a loan term.

TIF-LOCAL.name: Tax Increment Financing (Local)
TIF-LOCAL.description: Tax increment financing is local authority, not a state award. Municipal urban renewal authorities use the Urban Renewal Law (C.R.S. 31-25-101 et seq.); HB24-1172 added county revitalization authorities. Whether a district exists, and what it pays for, depends on a local plan and agreement.
TIF-LOCAL.note: Ask the local urban renewal authority or county whether a district covers the site.
TIF-LOCAL.source_note: Colorado General Assembly HB24-1172 page read 2026-10-26: title "County Revitalization Authorities"; "The act creates a process for the establishment of a county revitalization authority" and a plan "may provide for" tax increment financing. It is county authority, not municipal urban renewal, and not proof that any district funds housing. The former list of cities with active programs had no source and was removed. Funding type, rate, term, repayment and award are left blank.

CEO-WAP.name: Weatherization Assistance Program (Colorado / DOE WAP)
CEO-WAP.description: Income-qualified weatherization services administered through state and local WAP providers. DOE guidance confirms WAP is state/local administered and open to eligible homeowners and renters; no universal Colorado project-dollar amount is published for underwriting.
CEO-WAP.adminEntity: DOE / Colorado Energy Office / local WAP providers
CEO-WAP.source_note: Primary source reopened 2026-10-20: the DOE how-to-apply page still routes applicants through state administrators and local providers, with eligibility at 200% of the poverty guidelines or the LIHEAP 60% of state median income. DOE WAP pages previously checked 2026-07-18; Program Year 2026 guidance is published, but household/project awards vary by local provider. DOE describes delivered weatherization services, not one project-financing instrument. Funding type, interest rate, loan term, repayment and maximum award are left blank: no universal rental-project terms or cap are stated. Rechecked 2026-10-26: no material change on the program page.
CEO-WAP.warning: Screening context only. Verify local provider eligibility, landlord permission for renters, and current provider capacity before advising a household or underwriting a rehab scope.

CEO-IRA-HOME-ENERGY-REBATES.name: Colorado Home Energy Rebates (HEAR / HOMES)
CEO-IRA-HOME-ENERGY-REBATES.description: The Colorado Energy Office says the single-family appliance rebate (HEAR) is closed in both regions, rebates for small multifamily buildings will be available in 2026, and whole-home rebates (HER) will open to manufactured or mobile homes and large multifamily buildings in 2026. DOE describes the rebates as state-administered and available only in select states.
CEO-IRA-HOME-ENERGY-REBATES.source_note: Colorado Energy Office Home Energy Rebates page read 2026-10-20: "The HEAR single-family program is now closed for both Region 1 (the Front Range) and Region 2 (All Other Counties). Rebates for small multifamily buildings will be available in 2026." The Energy Office publishes the caps: appliance rebates (HEAR) up to $14,000 per household or unit; whole-home rebates (HER) for manufactured or mobile homes up to $16,000 below 80% AMI; and for large multifamily buildings up to $8,000 per unit below 80% AMI, or $4,000 per unit up to $400,000 per building at 80% AMI and above. These are per-unit or per-building caps that depend on income and expected energy savings, and the 2026 phases have no confirmed opening, so maximum award per project stays blank. DOE describes rebates rather than one of the loan/equity instruments; funding type, interest rate, loan term and repayment are left blank.
CEO-IRA-HOME-ENERGY-REBATES.warning: VERIFY before use. The single-family rebate is closed; the 2026 multifamily and manufactured-home phases have published caps but no confirmed opening.

CEO-SOLAR-FOR-ALL.name: Colorado Solar for All / GGRF watch
CEO-SOLAR-FOR-ALL.description: Colorado official federal-funds page records the original Solar for All award and planning intent, but EPA now states the Greenhouse Gas Reduction Fund authority and Solar for All implementation have been terminated/rescinded. Treat as a watch item, not available funding.
CEO-SOLAR-FOR-ALL.source_note: Colorado Energy Office Solar for All page read 2026-10-26: the program "is temporarily on hold due to recent developments at the federal level"; EPA terminated the national program in August 2025 and Colorado joined a multistate lawsuit on October 16, 2025. Not available funding. Funding type, rate, term, repayment and award are left blank; the historical award is not a balance.
CEO-SOLAR-FOR-ALL.warning: Do not count as available funding without fresh official confirmation; GGRF/Solar for All is rescission/litigation exposed.

CEO-BUILDING-ELECTRIFICATION-GRANTS.name: CEO building electrification / high-efficiency heating grants
CEO-BUILDING-ELECTRIFICATION-GRANTS.description: Colorado HB22-1362 created CEO-administered building electrification and high-efficiency electric heating/appliance grant authority for eligible entities including housing developers. Current open-round dollars were not fetch-verified on an accessible official CEO page this session.
CEO-BUILDING-ELECTRIFICATION-GRANTS.source_note: CEO High-Efficiency Electric Heating and Appliances grant page read 2026-10-26: "The Request for Applications is closed." "CEO is not currently accepting applications for this program." Program dates "July 1, 2022 - June 30, 2026" ($10.85 million total fund). HB22-1362 established the authority. Ended: not available funding.
CEO-BUILDING-ELECTRIFICATION-GRANTS.warning: Statutory program authority only. Verify any current NOFA, eligible uses, deadlines, and stacking rules before underwriting.

CEO-LBD-SHOWCASE.name: Large Building Decarbonization Showcase Grant Program
CEO-LBD-SHOWCASE.description: The Colorado Energy Office's LBD Showcase funds emissions cuts in large buildings covered by Building Performance Colorado. Round 1 awarded $7.2 million to 15 building owners on February 25, 2026. Round 2 is for implementation projects only: $500,000 to $2 million per award, covering 50 to 65% of implementation costs, with $8.5 million in total. CEO extended the Round 2 deadline to October 23, 2026.
CEO-LBD-SHOWCASE.source_note: CEO program page read 2026-10-21: "Amount: $500,000 - $2 million per award; 50 - 65% of the implementation costs up to $2 million with $8.5m in total funding available. Application Rounds: The deadline for Round 2 has been extended to October 23, 2026. Round 2 covers implementation only projects." The page also says CEO "will distribute $35 million across two funding rounds". Round 1: Governor's release of February 25, 2026 ("$7.2 million in grants", 15 awards), re-opened 2026-10-21. No later round is announced. Rechecked 2026-10-26: the Round 2 deadline of October 23, 2026 has passed and the page announces no later round.
CEO-LBD-SHOWCASE.warning: Retrofits of existing buildings covered by Building Performance Colorado only; not new construction. Round 2 closes October 23, 2026.

max_rule.text: $500,000 to $2 million per award, 50 to 65% of implementation costs, up to $2 million.

PROP123-LIHTC-GAP.name: Proposition 123 LIHTC Gap Finance
PROP123-LIHTC-GAP.description: Subordinate financing for developments awarded federal LIHTC that have not converted to permanent financing. Amortizing or non-amortizing structures depend on underwriting.

max_rule.text: Least of the loan supported at 1.05x DSCR on all must-pay debt, 10% of total project cost, or $6,000,000; minimum $400,000.

PROP123-LIHTC-GAP.source_note: Fixed rate is 2.5%. The page offers amortizing and non-amortizing structures without selecting one funding type or repayment schedule; these are left blank until underwriting. Loan term is not published; the greater-of-loan-term-or-30-years affordability covenant is not a stated loan term. The May 27–June 10, 2026 window closed; CHFA's October 19, 2026 notice says the next round takes applications October 21 to November 10, 2026 (5:00pm MT), with selections in December 2026. Most FY2027 gap money goes through the competitive tax credit rounds instead. Available, awarded and capacity balances for this instrument are not stated. Rechecked 2026-10-26: no material change on the program page.
restrictions: Restricted units average no more than 60% AMI.
Up to 25% of units may be unrestricted, but are excluded from eligible financing.
A jurisdiction affordable-housing commitment is required.

PROP123-EQUITY.name: Proposition 123 Equity
PROP123-EQUITY.description: Equity with returns from available cash flow and principal repayment deferred to a capital event or sale. Cannot be combined with federal or state Housing Tax Credit equity.

max_rule.text: Investment between $1,500,000 and $15,000,000, subject to project evaluation and available program funding.

PROP123-EQUITY.source_note: Below-market returns are cash-flow dependent; no numeric interest rate is stated. Principal is deferred to a capital event or sale; the investment term is up to 30 years. The 1% servicing charge is a share of available cash flow, not an interest rate. No current uncommitted balance is published. Last applications closed February 26, 2026.
restrictions: Cannot pair with federal or state Housing Tax Credit equity.
Restricted units average no more than 90% AMI.

CHFA-HOF.name: CHFA Housing Opportunity Fund
CHFA-HOF.description: Must-pay CHFA financing that can also support interest costs on CHFA senior debt. CHFA must be senior lender.
CHFA-HOF.source_note: Main loan requires monthly principal and interest, normally a 30-year term; longer terms are case-by-case. HOF may instead subsidize CHFA senior-debt interest costs. No numeric interest rate or remaining balance is published. CHFA must be senior lender.
restrictions: Interest support is an alternative use, not an additional $1 million award.

FHLB-TOPEKA-AHP.name: FHLBank Topeka Affordable Housing Program
FHLB-TOPEKA-AHP.description: Competitive AHP grant for eligible affordable housing through a participating member institution.

max_rule.text: No more than $1,500,000 per project and $75,000 per unit.

FHLB-TOPEKA-AHP.source_note: AHP is a grant, not interest-bearing project debt. Interest rate, loan term and repayment are left blank because the page does not publish a loan rate, loan term or one of the listed loan repayment structures; grant compliance and recapture rules still apply. Round opens July 1 and closes July 31, 2026; announcements no later than December 31. At least $29.3 million is a round allocation, not a current remaining balance.
